title: ECTODERMAL DYSPLASIA 17 WITH OR WITHOUT LIMB MALFORMATIONS

relationships.phenotype: ECTODERMAL DYSPLASIA 17 WITH OR WITHOUT LIMB MALFORMATIONS

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that ectodermal dysplasia-17 with or without limb malformations (ECTD17) is caused by heterozygous or homozygous mutation in the LEF1 gene on chromosome 4q25.

checks.claim: Ectodermal dysplasia-17 with or without limb malformations (ECTD17) is caused by heterozygous or homozygous mutation in the LEF1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Our findings establish mono- and biallelic variants in LEF1 as a cause for a novel syndrome comprising limb malformations and ectodermal dysplasia.
checks.explanation: Mono-/biallelic corresponds to heterozygous/homozygous; ECTD17 naming is nomenclature.

checks.claim: The LEF1 gene is located on chromosome 4q25.
checks.evidence_quote: We report two unrelated patients with 4q25 de novo deletion encompassing LEF1
checks.explanation: The deletion at 4q25 encompasses LEF1, so the gene is located at 4q25.

paragraphs.text: Ectodermal dysplasia-17 with or without limb malformations (ECTD17) is a disorder caused by alterations of LEF1, a transcription factor acting downstream of the WNT-beta-catenin signaling pathway. Ectodermal features include severe oligodontia of primary and permanent dentition, hypotrichosis, and hypohidrosis, and limb malformations can include radial ray defects, polydactyly, or split hand/foot. Inheritance can be autosomal dominant or autosomal recessive, depending on the type and location of the LEF1 variant (Levy et al., 2020; Dufour et al., 2022).

checks.explanation: The abstract links LEF1 haploinsufficiency to ectodermal dysplasia.

checks.claim: LEF1 is a transcription factor acting downstream of the WNT-beta-catenin signaling pathway.
checks.evidence_quote: Wnt/β-catenin pathway requires the lymphoid enhancer-binding factor 1 (LEF1), a nuclear mediator, to activate target gene expression.
checks.explanation: The abstract calls LEF1 a nuclear mediator that activates target genes for the Wnt/β-catenin pathway, which matches a downstream transcription factor.

paragraphs.text: In 11 affected individuals from 4 unrelated families with ectodermal dysplasia and/or limb malformations, Dufour et al. (2022) identified monoallelic variants in the LEF1 gene using high-throughput sequencing. In an affected individual from a consanguineous family, they identified a homozygous in-frame duplication in the LEF1 gene (c.69_71dupGAT; p.Met23dup). Functional studies, including immunofluorescence, immunoblotting, pulldown assays, and/or RNA sequencing, indicated that haploinsufficiency or loss of DNA binding was responsible for a mild to moderate phenotype, whereas loss of beta-catenin binding caused by biallelic variants was associated with a severe phenotype. Transcriptomic studies revealed an alteration of WNT signaling.
